Custom Image Translation API Function Description

⚠️ Note: This is an advanced feature that requires you to have basic API call knowledge.

1. Basic Description
This feature allows you to configure your own image translation API, supporting both GET and POST request methods. (For image translation, the POST Content-Type can be either application/json; charset=utf-8 or multipart/form-data. Simply select the appropriate Content-Type in the dropdown menu, and there’s no need to explicitly add it to the request headers below.) All API responses must be in JSON format.

2. Usage Scenarios
Typically, major translation API providers implement their own signature algorithms, making it impossible to integrate via simple GET/POST requests. As such, the practical use case for the custom image translation API is to connect with a translation API interface that you’ve built yourself.

3. Parameter Description
1、Request Method: Can be either GET or POST.
2、Content-Type (POST only): Can be application/json or multipart/form-data.
3、Base URL: Can specify http or https. If no scheme is specified, the default is https.
4、Query Parameters (GET only): Parameters appended to the base URL.
5、Request Headers: Headers sent with the request.
6、Request Body (POST only): Content included with the request.
7、JSON Response Path: Path to retrieve the translation result from the API response JSON.

Note:
1、In "Query Parameters" and the request body with Content-Type set to application/json, use "useimgbase64" to represent the image file to be translated.
2、In the request body with Content-Type set to multipart/form-data, use "useimgfile" to represent the image file to be translated.
3、Additionally, ensure that both "source language" and "target language" codes are included in the "Query Parameters" or "Request Body."

4. Request Examples
GET Request
Base URL:
https://api.example.com/translate

Query Parameters:
Key: img, Value: useimgbase64
Key: source, Value: ja
Key: target, Value: zh

Request Headers:
Authorization = my_custom_token

POST Request
Content-Type:
application/json

Base URL:
https://api.example.com/translate

Request Headers:
Authorization = my_custom_token

Request Body:
Key: img, Value: useimgbase64
Key: source, Value: ja
Key: target, Value: zh

POST Request
Content-Type:
multipart/form-data

Base URL:
https://api.example.com/translate

Request Headers:
Authorization = my_custom_token

Request Body:
Key: img, Value: useimgfile
Key: source, Value: ja
Key: target, Value: zh

5. JSON Response Path
Example 1:
Suppose the successful JSON response is as follows:

{
 "code": 0,
 "msg": "success",
 "data": {
 "translation": "Hello World"
 }
}

Then the JSON response path should be: "data.translation".

Example 2:
Suppose the successful JSON response is as follows:

{
 "code": 0,
 "msg": "success",
 "result": "Hello World"
}

Then the JSON response path should be: "result".(Excludes ".")

6. Before Using This Feature
You can first test the API response using tools like Postman or Reqable. Once the tests are successful, you can enter the relevant parameters into this feature.

Why is my HarmonyOS version 3.0 or greater, but it still says that the Android version is too low?

This is due to the fact that after Huawei updated HarmonyOS (note that it is not HarmonyOS NEXT), its underlying Android API can no longer be visually visible to users. For most newer Huawei phones, HarmonyOS 2.0 supports Android 10 (API 29). HarmonyOS 3.0 is compatible with Android 12 (API 31). However, for some older Huawei models, although HarmonyOS 3.0 has been updated, the underlying Android API has not been updated, and the underlying Android version of some models is still Android 10. As a result, the system still does not meet the requirements of Android 11 (API 30) for this software. Here are some of the known models:\n\nEquipped with Kirin 980 and below models, such as mate20, P30, Nova 5, etc., HarmonyOS 3.0 corresponds to Android version 10 (API 29). The HarmonyOS 3.0 of these models is not really 3.0, and there are many missing features, but the main upgrades are: updating the version number, using the new theme of 3.0, and adding some small features that do not depend on Android 12.
Why do I have granted accessibility permissions, but the software still prompts that I have not obtained accessibility permissions?

This is due to accessibility permissions being reclaimed by the system; Accessibility is a very important permission in Android. Most Android-based systems will revoke accessibility privileges when you exit the software or shut down and restart it, also for security reasons (of course, this software is open source and does not collect any information from you).\n\nKnowing the reason, it is also very easy to solve. As long as the software homepage clicks on the \"? > find the step to grant accessibility permissions - > click \"Go to grant this permission\" - > find the software, then turn off the accessibility permissions of the software, and re-grant them.
Adjust this option in the \"Translation Mode\" and \"API Configuration\" of the Settings page
Why did I click on the hoverball, but there was no translation result for a long time, and finally an error was reported?

This is most likely due to poor internet connections. Many waifu games need to use accelerators, but after using accelerators, it is relatively slow to access the domestic translation API. As a result, the translation will time out and errors will occur.\n\nAt this time, please turn off your wifi, turn on the data data, and then speed up with the accelerator again. At this point, you should be able to use the translation fluently. There is no need to worry about data consumption, generally speaking, when you use the translation mode of \"local OCR recognition + text translation\", the amount of traffic spent is minimal.
Why can\'t I download models, update the software, or see update announcements in the model management page?

This is because downloading models (GitHub/HuggingFace), checking for updates, and fetching announcements all require access to overseas services that are blocked in mainland China. Please enable or switch your VPN and try again. A stable proxy is recommended to ensure smooth network access.
I\'m getting a \"DataInspectionFailed\" or \"Output data may contain inappropriate content\" error during translation?

This is caused by the content safety review mechanism of the API platform. Translation platforms (such as Volc Engine, Tongyi Qianwen, etc.) may block sensitive content, and different platforms have different review thresholds.\n\nSolution: Try switching to a different translation platform or model. For example, switch from Volc Engine to DeepSeek or Tongyi Qianwen.
Manga translation results are missing, inaccurate, or slow?

You can try the following optimizations:

1. Frame the area that needs translation: Precisely selecting the text area improves OCR accuracy and avoids recognizing irrelevant content.

2. Reduce UI interference: Avoid selecting blank areas, game UI buttons, and other non-text content. Reducing unnecessary recognition improves speed.

3. Choose the right translation model: Models with mini, lit, or flash labels have faster response times.

In the manga translation debug mode, you can adjust the following parameters in real time via sliders. Changes take effect immediately and automatically apply to the normal translation flow. Parameters marked "v5 only" apply only to PP-OCRv5; "v6 only" applies only to PP-OCRv6; shared parameters are stored independently per engine.
[Detection Parameters (Det)]
1. det_thresh — Binarization Threshold (v6 only) v6 default: 0.3 | Range: 0.05 ~ 0.5
Text/background binarization threshold (DB internal segmentation map). Higher values → only keep high-confidence pixels (fewer boxes); lower values → more pixels classified as text (more boxes).
2. det_box_thresh — Detection Box Threshold v5 default: 0.3 | v6 default: 0.5 | Range: 0.1 ~ 0.9
Detection box retention threshold (bounding box score threshold). After synthesizing rectangles from the segmentation map, only boxes with scores above this value are kept. Higher → more precise boxes but possible missed detections; lower → higher recall but possible noise.
• Text frequently missed → lower (e.g. v5: 0.2, v6: 0.3) • Too many noise boxes → raise (e.g. v5: 0.4, v6: 0.7)
3. det_unclip_ratio — Box Expansion Ratio v5 default: 1.6 | v6 default: 1.6 | Range: 1.0 ~ 3.0
Detection box outward expansion factor. When synthesizing rectangles from the segmentation region, boxes are expanded by this factor to avoid hugging the text edges too tightly. Higher → looser boxes (good for tightly packed characters); lower → more compact boxes.
• Recognition results have missing/truncated characters → increase (e.g. 2.0) • Boxes too large, causing overlaps → decrease (e.g. 1.2)
4. use_dilation — Segmentation Dilation (v6 only) v6 default: On
Whether to apply dilation processing to the detection segmentation map. Dilation merges adjacent text into a single region (good for dense text); disable to keep the original segmentation. Recommended to keep enabled for vertical manga text.
5. limit_side_len — Detection Side Length Limit (v6 only) v6 default: 736 | Range: 64 ~ 2048 (pixels)
Image side length limit during detection. The input image is scaled if its side exceeds this value. Higher → more accurate detection but slower; lower → faster but may lose detail.
6. limit_type — Side Limit Strategy (v6 only) v6 default: min (limit shortest side)
Whether limit_side_len applies to the minimum or maximum side. min = limit the shortest side (preserve detail); max = limit the longest side (prioritize speed).
[Recognition Parameters (Rec)]
7. text_score — Recognition Confidence Threshold v5 default: 0.5 | v6 default: 0.5 | Range: 0.1 ~ 0.9
Text recognition result confidence threshold. Results below this score are discarded. Higher → only keep high-confidence results (fewer but more accurate); lower → keep more results (more but possibly incorrect).
• Translation frequently missing → lower (e.g. 0.3) • Translation has garbled/wrong text → raise (e.g. 0.6)
8. rec_batch_num — Recognition Batch Size (v6 only) v6 default: 6 | Range: 1 ~ 32
Text recognition batch inference size. Each batch processes N text lines simultaneously. Higher values improve throughput but use more memory; lower values use less memory but are slower.
[Classification Parameters (Cls)]
9. cls_thresh — Orientation Classification Threshold (v6 only) v6 default: 0.9 | Range: 0.5 ~ 1.0
Text orientation classification confidence threshold. Text lines with classification scores below this value are not flipped (keep original orientation). Higher → only flip high-confidence upside-down text; lower → more lines may be flipped. Relevant for vertical or rotated text scenarios.
[v5-Only Parameters]
10. large_box_enabled — Large Box Filter (v5 only) v5 default: Off
Filters detection boxes that occupy too much of the image. In some scenarios (manga backgrounds, decorative patterns), the detector may mistakenly identify large areas as text. When enabled, boxes whose width, height, or area exceeds a certain ratio of the image are discarded.
• Large false-positive boxes appearing → enable • Normal use: keep disabled
11. large_box_ratio — Large Box Filter Threshold (v5 only) v5 default: 60% | Range: 30% ~ 80%
Threshold for the large box filter. Detection boxes whose width, height, or area exceed this ratio of the image are discarded. Only effective when large box filter is enabled.
• Filtering too aggressive (normal boxes discarded) → increase ratio • Not filtering enough (large boxes still appear) → decrease ratio
What is the purpose of downloading dedicated OCR recognition models?

PP-OCRv5's Chinese recognition model (rec_zh) is a Chinese-Japanese-English general model that can recognize Chinese, Japanese, and English. When no dedicated model is downloaded, English recognition uses this general model by default.

After downloading a dedicated model, the system automatically switches for better results:

• English model (rec_en): Optimized for English, higher accuracy especially for uppercase/lowercase, numbers, and punctuation.
• Korean model (rec_ko): Dedicated to Korean. Without it, Korean text cannot be recognized.
• Russian model (rec_ru): Dedicated to Russian/Cyrillic script. Without it, Russian text cannot be recognized.

How to download: Go to Settings → Model Management → PP-OCRv5 Recognition Models, tap download. Models are small (7~13MB) and take effect immediately without restarting.

How to verify: When translating manga in a non-default language (e.g. English), a toast notification "使用专用识别模型: rec_en" will appear at the bottom of the screen, confirming the dedicated model is active. If no notification appears, the general Chinese model is still being used.
Models fail to download - how to manually download and place them in the correct directory?

If automatic download is not working, you can manually download the model files and place them in the correct location.

Model storage path base: Android/data/com.moe.starflow/files/

1. PP-OCRv5 core (det + rec_zh)
 Directory: ppocrv5/
 ├── det_v5.onnx → Browser (Detection model ~4.6MB)
 ├── rec_zh.onnx → Browser (Recognition model ~16MB)
 └── rec_zh_dict.txt → Browser (Dictionary ~75KB)

2. PP-OCRv5 optional languages
 Directory: ppocrv5/
 ├── rec_en.onnx + rec_en_dict.txt (English ~7.5MB)
 ├── rec_ko.onnx + rec_ko_dict.txt (Korean ~12.9MB)
 └── rec_ru.onnx + rec_ru_dict.txt (Russian ~7.7MB)

3. PP-OCRv6 medium (det + rec)
 Directory: ppocrv6/
 ├── det_v6_medium.onnx → Browser (~60MB)
 └── rec_v6_medium.onnx → Browser (~74MB)

4. RT-DETR-V2
 Directory: rt_detr/
 └── model.onnx → Browser (~11MB)

5. manga-ocr
 Directory: manga_ocr_download/
 ├── encoder_model.onnx → Browser (~85MB)
 ├── decoder_model.onnx → Browser (~50MB)
 └── vocab.txt → Browser (~200KB)

You can click the 🔗 Browser button next to each model to open the download link. After downloading, move the files to the corresponding folder using a file manager. If the folder does not exist, create it yourself.

Uni AI Translation API Function Description

⚠️ Note: This is an advanced feature that requires you to have basic API call knowledge.

1. Basic Description
This feature allows you to use mainstream AI services for translation (as long as they are compatible with OpenAI API specifications), such as ChatGPT, Qwen, DeepSeek, etc. The integration method is through calling official API interfaces.

2. Parameter Description
1. API_KEY: The API key provided by the official website
2. Base URL: The access endpoint provided by the official website 
3. Model: The name of the model to be used
4. System Prompt: Sets the identity for the model, keep default is recommended
5. User Prompt: Translation instructions sent to the model, keep default is recommended

3. Configuration Example
Taking the integration of Alibaba's "Qwen-Plus" model as an example:
For API_KEY, fill in normally;
For Base URL, Alibaba's Qwen models generally use https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1;
For Model, the "Qwen-Plus" model corresponds to the code name qwen-plus;
For System Prompt and User Prompt, keep the defaults.

4. Before Using This Feature
You can first test the API response using tools like Postman, Reqable, etc. After successful testing, fill in the relevant parameters into this feature.
